title: Diffuse lung disease and HRCT

steps.tx: The **Usual interstitial pneumonia** (UIP) HRCT pattern is characterized by basal and subpleural predominance with coarse reticular opacities, architectural distortion, and traction bronchiectasis. Pathognomonic **honeycombing**, presenting as clustered, thick-walled cystic spaces arranged in multiple layers beneath the pleura, confirms UIP without requiring surgical lung biopsy.

vis.caption: Honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis in fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis, beside perilymphatic sarcoid nodules

steps.tx: **Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia** (NSIP) presents on thoracic HRCT with bilateral, symmetrical ground-glass opacities accompanied by fine reticulation and lower-lobe traction bronchiectasis. Immediate **subpleural sparing** along the dorsal aspect of the lower lung zones is a classic discriminator differentiating cellular and fibrotic NSIP from the peripheral subpleural destruction of UIP.

steps.tx: Chronic **hypersensitivity pneumonitis** predominantly involves the mid and upper lung zones with poorly defined centrilobular micronodules and mosaic attenuation. Expiratory HRCT demonstrates lobular air-trapping, producing the pathognomonic **three-density sign** (headcheese sign) characterized by adjacent normal attenuation, low-attenuation air-trapping, and high-attenuation ground-glass infiltrates.
steps.say: Chronic hypersensitivity pneumonitis predominantly involves the mid and upper lung zones with poorly defined centrilobular micronodules and mosaic attenuation. Expiratory HRCT demonstrates lobular air-trapping, producing the pathognomonic three-density sign, also called headcheese sign, characterized by adjacent normal attenuation, low-attenuation air-trapping, and high-attenuation ground-glass infiltrates.

left.title: Three-Density Sign Components
points: Indicates mixed infiltrative and small-airway disease

steps.tx: **Lymphangioleiomyomatosis** (LAM) occurs almost exclusively in women of reproductive age and patients with tuberous sclerosis complex. HRCT reveals diffusely distributed, round, uniform, thin-walled **lung cysts** surrounded by normal intervening lung parenchyma, typically accompanied by preserved or hyperinflated lung volumes, recurrent pneumothoraces, and chylous pleural effusions.

vis.alt: Computed tomography of the chest demonstrating round thin-walled uniform lung cysts in lymphangioleiomyomatosis
vis.caption: Thin-walled uniform round cysts with normal intervening lung in LAM

steps.tx: Pulmonary **Langerhans cell histiocytosis** exhibits a profound predilection for young adults with a history of cigarette **smoking** exceeding 95% of cases. Early nodular inflammation centered on bronchioles cavitates into bizarre, irregularly shaped, bilobed or cloverleaf cysts that selectively involve the upper and mid lung zones while strictly sparing the lung bases.

left.title: PLCH Cyst Features
points: Evolves from centrilobular nodules to cysts

right.title: LAM Cyst Features
points: Involves costophrenic angles and lung bases

steps.tx: **Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis** is characterized by the accumulation of periodic acid-Schiff positive phospholipid surfactant within alveolar spaces. Thoracic CT demonstrates a pathognomonic **crazy-paving** pattern consisting of sharply demarcated, patchy ground-glass attenuation with superimposed smooth thickening of both interlobular and intralobular septa.

vis.alt: CT chest demonstrating geographic ground-glass attenuation with interlobular septal thickening
vis.caption: Classic crazy-paving pattern in pulmonary alveolar proteinosis

steps.tx: Thoracic **Sarcoidosis** classically produces symmetric bilateral hilar and right paratracheal lymphadenopathy alongside a distinct **perilymphatic** micronodular distribution. Well-defined non-caseating granulomatous nodules cluster along bronchovascular bundles, subpleural surfaces, interlobar fissures, and interlobular septa, exhibiting mid-to-upper lung zone predominance with progressive perihilar fibrotic distortion.

steps.tx: Chronic **Silicosis** manifests as multiple small, sharply circumscribed nodular opacities with upper lobe and posterior segment predominance. These nodules may coalesce into progressive massive fibrosis, frequently accompanied by pathognomonic peripheral **eggshell calcification** outlining the capsules of enlarged hilar and mediastinal lymph nodes.
